Vice President JD Vance blamed the Biden administration for the record $40 trillion U.S. national debt, but his Thursday night comments partially backfired, with many social media users expressing fatigue at the blame-shifting between administrations.

Speaking on Newsmax, Vance said: "Even though the debt is too high, even though we inherited this debt bomb from the Biden administration, we actually do have a plan to grow the economy faster than the debt."

He continued: "The problem during the Biden administration, which we are still dealing with today, is that the debt was growing faster than U.S. GDP — that is the crux of the issue."

The U.S. national debt surpassed the $40 trillion mark this week, having reached $38 trillion in October. The national debt has continued to grow across multiple presidential administrations, with both Democrats and Republicans bearing responsibility.

According to Reuters, the U.S. national debt increased by $8.4 trillion during Biden's four-year term, while it rose by $11.6 trillion across Trump's two terms so far.

Vance previewed on Thursday that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has a "very prudent plan," claiming the administration is "on track" to drive U.S. economic growth to outpace the ballooning national debt.

The vice president's appearance on Newsmax was promptly mocked online, with critics pointing to the Trump administration's own spending issues.
